# Panel J2 verdict, round 3: first-time visitor

Judged from the 2-second clip sheets (reader 1440 and reader 1024) plus the static scene sheets at 1440. Visitor scrolled ~250 px/s and paused 2 s at each heading. Scores are 0-10.

## Headline

- Would keep scrolling: **77.6%** of screens at 1440 (38 of 49) and **77.8%** at 1024 (42 of 54). Same shape at both widths. The last screen of the page is counted as a yes (nothing left to scroll, the sign-off is satisfying).
- Scores: keepScrolling **7.0**, tempo **6.3**, discovery **6.0**.
- The page is two things. The film-led parts (opening flight, the sea journey, the film plates, the Red Dead valley, the Marauder's Map, the ending) pull me along at 100% yes. The document-led middle (About, the Workshop project cards, the kill-list) is where I stop wanting to scroll: 0% on About and the kill-list, 44-64% on the project cards.
- Discovery is the weakest leg: the egg counter and the explicit "Take off" pill invite play, but the hints are tiny and nothing responds in the first minutes.

## 2. Tempo

- **Opening: play screen, broomstick flight, name, hero: medium.** Flight is brisk (about 6 s from Play to the name) and thrilling, then ~10 s parked on a nearly still hero. Great first impression, slightly long hold.
- **The Crossing (Pirates): ship arrival and contents card: medium.** Iris reveal is cinematic; the ship then sits ~6 s and the contents card is quiet. Calm, not dull.
- **The Crossing: 'A builder of quantitative systems' (about): slow.** A wall of small serif that does not move. The first place the page stops being a film and becomes a document.
- **The Crossing: how the methodology was earned (sea journey): medium.** Best-paced stretch. The sea picture changes with each step and the copy is short, so scroll and picture move together.
- **The Workshop (3 Idiots): lecture hall, pen, gauntlet board: medium.** Teal wave wipe into the classroom is lovely; then a 6-8 s static reading hold before the chalkboard gauntlet wakes it up.
- **The Workshop: project cards, blueprint, thesis chart, drone, 'what I can do': slow.** A grind. The same card (small text, murky photo) repeats; blueprints, the circled stats and the drone photo are the only lifts.
- **The Workshop: the kill-list: slow.** A mono-type list scrolled past; reads like a spreadsheet. Plodding.
- **Three films and a game: hub card and film plates: brisk.** One plate every ~4 s, each a big picture and one line. The pace I wanted everywhere.
- **The Frontier (Red Dead): dawn to golden hour, three arenas, silhouette, satchel, WANTED poster: medium.** Dark gap, then a long hold on the golden valley (~10 s), then it speeds up with the paper map, satchel and poster.
- **Writing: 'Thinking in public, soon.' cream journal: medium.** Bright cream page is a shock and the opening is sparse; entries with pencil sketches then move quickly.
- **Voices: 'In their words.' campfire quotes: slow.** ~10 s of small italic quotes on a held campfire image. Sincere but static.
- **The Light (Harry Potter): Great Hall and the Marauder's Map principles: medium.** Great Hall hold, then a parchment unfolds; principle cards read at a steady, pleasant pace. The title card hold is a touch long.
- **Contact and credits: medium.** Clear ask, short credit roll, 'Mischief managed.' A gentle landing.

Overall: the page alternates cinematic beats (brisk or medium) with reading holds (slow). The best pace is the film plate section (one picture and one line every ~4 s). The worst is the 2-minute Workshop run from "Led by what survived scrutiny." to the end of the kill-list, where the same card layout repeats and several clips in a row are identical frames.

What worked: the Play button, the "Take off" pill and the film chips are unmistakable. The egg counter is a good promise. What did not: the counter stayed at 0/12 for the whole scroll, the Dead Eye tag and the compass explain themselves only if you read tiny type, and nothing near the hero says "try me" in plain words.
